name: development-opentofu
description: Infrastructure-as-code topic plugin for cloud provisioning — OpenTofu and Terraform-compatible HCL: .tf/.tf.json sources, module structure, provider and version constraints, backend and state configuration, and .tfvars hygiene. Composes ALONGSIDE a language plugin, and can itself be PRIMARY for a repo with no application language (a provisioning repo). Charter — mechanism only: run the static checks, plus the consumer's own Conftest policies from policies/conftest/**/*.rego (the policy step alone skips when no file matches; the static checks always run). One opinion is held as a first-class check rather than left to a consumer policy: state must be encrypted at rest — checked dialect-aware, not one dialect's block, and binding only where the repo owns state. Defers what the modules deploy INTO a cluster to development-kubernetes, and images and application code to the language plugins (language-first); the boundary is the file set, so cluster resources expressed in HCL stay here. Ships no approver agent — a provisioning change can destroy state no rollback recovers, so a human approves. Named for the MPL-2.0 tool; BUSL-licensed Terraform is supported, not endorsed. This slice is the skeleton: the ownership boundary and the marketplace registration (#1159). The gather script, topic marker and dispatcher (#1160), the four agents and the review panel (#1161), the bootstrap check pipeline (#1162), and the self-contained test fixtures (#1163) follow.
